summary: The most probable cause is a degradation in broker-gateway (or its upstream broker) on GET /orders/status starting at 10:00. Its error rate jumped from baseline and latency rose from ~220ms to a ~696ms peak, and both order-router and orchestrator began logging broker-gateway HTTP 503s within the same minute, with no recovery by 10:29. This is consistent with synchronous order calls failing or timing out, leaving orders 'order pending' and prompting customer retries. The 09:50 order-router deploy was a log-level tweak and is not supported as the cause: error rate and latency showed no step at deploy time and first moved at 10:00. Where the 503s originate (broker-gateway itself, its upstream, or an external vendor) is not established, and retry amplification and queue-side delays were not verified.

hypotheses.statement: broker-gateway (or its upstream broker) is degrading on GET /orders/status from 10:00, returning 503s and slow responses to both order-router and orchestrator, so synchronous order calls fail or time out, orders stay 'order pending' and customers retry.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: broker-gateway err_rate was at baseline at 09:59 and jumped at 10:00, and latency rose from ~220ms to 331ms at 10:00, peaking at ~696ms at 10:04. Both were still elevated at the end of the window.
broker-gateway logged its first slow GET /orders/status WARN at 10:00:03, about 29 seconds before order-router's first 503 at 10:00:32. Slowness on that endpoint rose over 10:01-10:04.

Both of broker-gateway's callers, order-router and orchestrator, log broker-gateway HTTP 503s from the onset and continue through the end of the window. This points to a common origin rather than a single caller's fault.
No change was recorded for broker-gateway, and its request rate was flat, so a load spike does not explain the degradation.
It is likely that the slow /orders/status endpoint and the resulting 503s are what keep orders in 'order pending'. This link is an assumption, since the confirmation hop is not verified in the graph.

contradicting.text: broker-gateway's own logs contain no ERROR or 503 lines, so it is not shown that broker-gateway returned the 503s. They may originate upstream of it, at an external broker, or at a boundary without a log line.
The cause of the slowness is unknown. broker-gateway has no visible callees, and no vendor or broker maintenance information was available.
The origin of the 503s rests on assumptions. The 20-second ordering between order-router and orchestrator is within possible clock skew.

The only past-incident match (INC-0431) was a validation regression with a different symptom. It is a hint only and is not evidence about this outage.

hypotheses.statement: Retry amplification from customer and possibly order-router retries adds load to an already slow broker-gateway, sustaining the elevated errors and producing duplicate submissions; it is an amplifier, not the trigger.
hypotheses.label: low

contradicting.text: Order-router request rate and broker-gateway request rate were both flat, so no volume spike is visible. Retries as an amplifier are therefore not demonstrated.

It is plausible that customer retries produce duplicate submissions, but retries and duplicate order IDs were never measured. This is an unverified assumption, and at most retries are an amplifier rather than the trigger.

hypotheses.statement: The 'order pending' state sits in the queue-based confirmation path (inbound-msgs consumed by orchestrator, or portfolio-updates), where a backlog or consumer problem delays confirmations independently of the broker-gateway failure.
hypotheses.label: low

The metrics for inbound-msgs and portfolio-updates could not be checked, since rabbitmq exposes no per-queue depth or consumer metrics and the dependency lookup returned no edges. A queue-side delay is therefore not ruled out, only unsupported.

assumptions.text: broker-gateway (or its own upstream) is the likely origin of the 503s and timeouts, since order-router only reports failures calling it. This is not yet verified, and I did not query broker-gateway logs.

The order-router to broker-gateway to postgres path is the synchronous order-placement path. The graph does not show orchestrator calling order-router, so the exact order confirmation hop is unverified.

INC-0431 differs from the current case: its symptom was placement errors (validation regression), while the current report is orders stuck in 'order pending' after placement with customer retries, which may point to a downstream confirmation or queue delay rather than validation.
broker-gateway is degrading on its own (or on its upstream) starting at 10:00, and the slow GET /orders/status endpoint may delay the 'order pending' state customers see.

Because orchestrator fails with the same broker-gateway 503s starting within the same minute, the common origin is probably broker-gateway or its upstream, not order-router's deploy. The 20-second ordering is within possible clock skew, so it does not establish which caller failed first.

Order confirmation may run through portfolio-updates (aa-sync to portfolio-consumer) or through orchestrator's inbound-msgs consumption, but the graph has no edge linking these queues to order placement or to a confirmation step, so this remains unverified.

The 503 source is still unresolved. The broker-gateway logs describe slowness and do not mention a 503 or an error, so the failure may originate upstream of broker-gateway, or the 503 may be generated at the broker-gateway boundary without a log line.

Because broker-gateway has no recorded change and no visible callees, a change inside broker-gateway is unlikely to be the trigger. The 503s may originate at an external broker or vendor, which these tools cannot see.

actions.text: Escalate to the broker or vendor and check their status page for an incident or maintenance around 10:00. In parallel, engage the broker-gateway owners to check its upstream connectivity.
actions.rationale: The degradation began at 10:00 on broker-gateway's GET /orders/status with no recorded change on broker-gateway, and it persisted through 10:29. Our tools cannot see the external broker.

actions.text: Do not roll back the 09:50 order-router deploy as a remedy. Only revisit it if broker-gateway checks come back clean.
actions.rationale: Order-router's metrics were flat across the deploy, and orchestrator fails against broker-gateway in the same way without that deploy.

actions.text: Consider tightening order-router and web-app retry behaviour, or applying temporary throttling or customer-facing messaging, to limit duplicate submissions while broker-gateway is degraded. Measure duplicate order IDs first.
actions.rationale: Customers are retrying while orders are pending. Duplicates are plausible but unmeasured, so this should be confirmed before changing behaviour.

actions.text: Add broker-gateway alerting on /orders/status latency and 5xx rate, and review timeout, retry and circuit-breaker settings for order-router and orchestrator calls to broker-gateway.
actions.rationale: The degradation affected both callers and was sustained for at least 30 minutes, and there is a gradual latency rise that earlier alerting could catch.
